主题: SpaceX Material Control and Traceability Expectations

实体: company:SpaceX, product:Starship, project:mission, product:Raptor, person:You, person:Buyer, person:Supplier Development Engineer

内容:
Dear SpaceX Partners,
First, we want to extend our congratulations to you all for the success of Starship’s Flight 10! This achievement could not have been possible without the dedication, hard work, and commitment to excellence from each of you. We thank you for the critical role you play in our mission.
That said, we want to address a recent issue that highlights the importance of unwavering process discipline. Raw material was recently sourced in the incorrect condition (temper) and progressed all the way through to SpaceX production. While this specific issue was caught in testing, it underscores one of the most significant risks to our mission:
insufficient material controls
.
At SpaceX, the integrity of every part and material we fly is non-negotiable. A single lapse in process controls or traceability has the potential to compromise human safety and the reliability of our vehicle. We rely on you as partners to ensure that you and your teams are operating with the same uncompromising standards.
This incident should serve as an opportunity to rigorously re-examine every step of our processes. From raw material sourcing, manufacturing, sub-tier suppliers, to final delivery, there must be airtight traceability with no room for error. We ask that you:
Audit
each stage of your process for potential failure modes, especially taking a hard look at all material control, traceability systems, and incoming inspection. Implement corrective actions expediently as needed to make the process robust.
Reinforce accountability
across your organization to eliminate every possible opportunity for failure. This should felt by everybody in the company.
Enforce proper traceability documentation
throughout the process. As a supplier for the Starship, Raptor, and/or Falcon/Dragon programs, you are required to utilize eCerts. Please work with your buyer to get set up if you haven’t already, and ensure all shipments utilize eCerts with all proper documentation. Take eCert rejections seriously and fix the root cause.
Escalate immediately
to your Supplier Development Engineer or Buyer if any risk to conformance or traceability is identified.
Prioritize timely and high quality PPAP submissions
(Production Part Approval Process) when required.
Please enforce this consistently, and ensure every member of your team understands these expectations. Don’t hesitate to reach out to myself or your Supply Chain contacts if you have any questions or concerns. Thank you again for your continued partnership on our ambitious goals, and for treating this matter with the attention it deserves.
